qAndA.answer: The video starts with a Pensive mood, highlighting the problems of the old world. It transitions to an Excited mood as it presents the potential of a new civilization and the power of collaborative innovation. The mood becomes more Pensive again in Scenes 7 and 8 as the complexities of social change and activism are explored. Finally, the video ends on a Hopeful note, emphasizing the opportunity for positive change through collective action.
qAndA.question: How does the video's mood change throughout the narrative?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Let's face it, the world has broken and many of the institutions that have served us well
for decades or even centuries have come to the end of their life cycle.
From newspapers, record labels, and old models of financial services to our energy grid,
transportation systems, and institutions for global cooperation and problem solving.
The industrial economy has finally run out of gas.
We're at a turning point in human history.
At the same time, the contours of a new kind of civilization are becoming clear, as millions
of connected citizens begin to forge alternative institutions, using the web as a platform
for innovation and value creation.
From education and science to new approaches to citizen engagement and democracy, sparkling
new initiatives are underway, embracing a new set of principles for the 21st century.
Collaboration, openness, sharing, interdependence, and integrity.
This finally happening, with the proliferation of social media and social networks, we all
have at our fingertips the most powerful tools and platform ever for growth, prosperity,
social development, and a just and sustainable world.
Social media is becoming social production.
In every industry from all walks of life, people are self-organizing, taking us from collaborative
innovation in business that we first discuss when we wrote WICANOMICS to macro-wicANOMICS,
the art and science of collaboration to change the world, like the printing press before
at the new media are enabling nothing less than the birth of a new civilization.
Renovating science in healthcare with patients like me, where 80,000 patients are crowdsourcing
their data to help doctors, scientists, and their own course of treatment.
In Kenya, Ushahidi, a text messaging platform created to document election violence, has
grown from helping emergency response teams in Haiti during the earthquake, to helping
emergency snow removal in Washington, and even the BBC during the Tube Strike in London.
With Galaxy Zoo, 275,000 teachers and students are reinventing science and education by helping
astronomers discover and map new galaxies.
Network models of the newspaper are providing good journalism, investigative reporting,
and ensuring that journals get paid.
Old-style radio is collapsing, TV is becoming nothing less than a cool new app, and the failing
music industry is being replaced by streaming audio that gives access to millions of songs
with fair compensation to musicians and to songwriters.
Teachers, professors, and students are using the internet to reinvent education from the
industrial model where teachers lecture and students are passive recipients of knowledge
to student-focused collaborative learning customized to the needs of the learner.
The wiki revolution sweeping the Middle East are harbingers of change.
Social media didn't cause the Arab Spring and Justice did.
Social media didn't create the revolutions.
They were created by a new generation that no longer wanted to be treated as subjects,
but just as the internet drops collaboration costs in business, so it also drops the
cost of dissent of rebellion and even insurrection.
Social change is in the air, perhaps like never before.
Occupy Wall Street is the tip of the iceberg of a global movement for a world that's fair
and just.
The Coney 2012 video was seen by over 100 million people in a week, and the one hand that
led to a movement that caused the U.S. Congress to take action and help hunt down the brutal
warlord.
But on the other, it raises tough issues about these networks.
There are accountability, there are legitimacy, there are representation and leadership.
Things that are new generation of social innovators and activists must address.
This is a time of danger, but fundamentally it's a time of profound change and of great
opportunity, and we can achieve a new age of promise fulfilled, but only if we get involved.
Which is why I, along with Anthony Williams, wrote macro-wikonomics.
We hope that the book will be your field guide to forge new solutions for our connected
planet.
Let's do this.

youtube_description:
Macrowikinomics: Novas soluções para um Planeta Conectado.

Agora disponível emPaperback em http://macrowikinomics.com

Nesta nova era da inteligência em rede, comunidades colaborativas estão melhorando e até mesmo ultrapassadno as instituições em frangalhos.Estamos inovando a forma nossas instituições financeiras e governos operaram; como educamos nossos filhos; como as indústrias de saúde, jornais e energia servem seus clientes;como cuidamos dos nossos bairros, e até mesmo como vamos resolver os problemas globais.

De seu mais recente livro, Macrowikinomics: Novas soluções para um Planeta Conectado, co-autores Don Tapscott e Anthony D. Williams apresentam inovações de todos os cantos do mundo: como as empresas, organizações e indivíduos estão usando a colaboração em massa para revolucionar não só a forma como nós trabalhamos, mas como vivemos, aprendemos, criamos e cuidamos uns dos outros.

Don Tapscott é uma das maiores autoridades mundiais em inovação, mídia e do impacto econômico e social da tecnologia. Ele aconselha empresas e líderes de governo ao redor do mundo. 

Em 2011, Don foi nomeado um dos mais influentes pensadores de gestão do mundo pela Thinkers50. Ele é autor ou co-autor de 14 livros lidos, incluindo os best-sellers de 1997 Wikinomics: Como a Colaboração em Massa Muda Tudo. 

Ele é o presidente da Insight Moxie, membro do Fórum Econômico Mundial, Professor Adjunto da Escola de Rotman de Gestão e Fellow do Martin Prosperity Institute . 

Saiba mais em http://dontapscott.com and http://twitter.com/dtapscott

Anthony D. Williams é autor de best-sellers, orador e consultor que ajuda organizações em todo o mundo aproveitar o poder da inovação colaborativa em empresas, governo e sociedade.

Anthony é professor visitante da Universidade deToront,o Escola Munk de Assuntos Globais e membro sênior para a inovação com o Conselho de Lisboa, em Bruxelas. Saiba mais em http://anthonydwilliams.com e http://twitter.com /adw_tweets
